english.title: Adult attempt to meet boy under 16 following sexual grooming - SOA 2003
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person aged 18 or over, namely **(..SPECIFY OFFENDER'S AGE..), having on at least two earlier occasions met or communicated with a boy under the age of 16, namely **(..SPECIFY VICTIM'S AGE..), not reasonably believing he was aged 16 or over,

(A)_[you attempted to meet him]_
(B)_[you attempted to travel with the intention to meet him]_
(C)_[you attempted to meet him]_

and you intended to do something to or in respect of him, during or after the meeting which would have involved the commission by you of a relevant offence, as defined in section 15(2)(b) of the Sexual Offences Act 2003, namely **(..SPECIFY THE RELEVANT OFFENCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) of the Criminal Attempts Act 1981.

investigatoraction.description: Attracts liability for entry on sex offenders register

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
This offence wording is now OBSOLETE in view of changes made to section of the Act by section 73 of and Schedule 15 to the Criminal Justice and Immigration Act 2008 - Now see SX03211 and H9363.

(i) An act done by a person in a country or territory outside the United Kingdom which, constituted an offence under the law in force in that country or territory, and would constitute a sexual offence to which this section applies if it had been done in England and Wales or in Northern Ireland, constitutes that sexual offence under the law of that part of the United Kingdom, and provided that person was on 01/09/1997, or who has since become a British citizen or resident in the United Kingdom he/she may have proceedings brought against them in the United Kingdom. (section 72).
(ii) A person convicted of this offence is subject to notification and orders as provided by section 80 of the Act. (Sch 3 paragraph 24).

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
Indictment: Ten years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
